false will do nothing - a user handler has to manage the buffer by itself. If it doesn't, the inbound buffer will probably grow infinitly.

I found a problem with calling `discard(Some)ReadBytes()` in our core.

`ReplayingDecoder` for example keeps its own index variable called `checkpoint`.  Let's assume that the decoder is the first inbound handler in the pipeline (which is often the case).
- `AioSocketChannel` calls `discardReadBytes()` on every read.  If the `readerIndex` of the cumulation buffer is non-zero, `checkpoint` will go out of sync.  It's interesting that we didn't reproduce this bug at all so far.
- `AbstractChannel.expandReadBuffer()` also calls `discardReadBytes()` if the inbound buffer reaches at its maximum capacity and no writable bytes are left. Again, it will make `checkpoint` go out of sync.

The simplest yet inflexible solution would be force `ReplayingDecoder` to ensure `inboundAutoDiscard` is always `true`. Same restriction must be applied on any abstract decoders that keeps its own index variables, and I think it will be pretty error prone.

A less user-friendly solution would be not calling `discard(Some)ReadBytes()` at all from core & abstract decoders.  This will increase the risk of boundlessly growing buffer.

Let me keep thinking about possible solutions. Feel free to share your idea.
No useful idea from me yet. Anyone?
I think the last idea is most elegant, but I guess it will have some performance penalty and some people might find it less intuitive.
Considering the user-friendliness, adding `ChannelInboundHandler.trimInboundBuffer()` sounds like the best so far in my opinion.
@trustin can you give more details on ChannelInboundHandler.trimInboundBuffer() I don't get it :/

Sure.  Currently, for example, `ChannelInboundByteHandlerAdapter` calls `in.discardReadBytes()`.  I want to move this to `DefaultChannelPipeline` (or `DefaultChannelHandlerContext`) so that the pipeline trims the inbound buffer between every `inbountBufferUpdated()` events.  To give more control over buffer trimming, `ChannelInboundHandler.trimInboundBuffer()` could be added and its default implementation will usually be `in.discardSomeReadBytes()`.

A stateful decoder with an index member variable could override/implement `trimInboundBuffer()` to adjust the index member variable accordingly.
Also, `trimInboundBuffer()` could be a solution for #805
